verdict.rationale: The IRS runs its own machine-to-machine channels that can be automated headlessly: MeF is a system-to-system XML e-file channel, IRIS has an Application to Application intake, and the ATS test environment is separate from Production, which suits CI-style validation. All of these are credential-gated, though: provider enrollment can take up to 45 days and may require fingerprinting, IRIS A2A needs a Transmitter Control Code, schemas and WSDLs are only available to registered users, and ATS opens only in seasonal windows. Taxpayer-facing flows such as the EIN assistant, Online Account and the online 83(b) form require ID.me biometric liveness checks or return 403 to agents. Missing for 10: a public, self-serve API or CLI for headless use, always-available CI test access without the enrollment wait, automatable flows for EIN, 83(b) and account services, and public machine-readable interface definitions (OpenAPI or downloadable schemas).
